statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Connections progress through three phases: initiation, including a three-way handshake; data transfer; and termination.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Connections progress through three phases: initiation, including a three-way handshake; data transfer; and termination.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Connections progress through three phases: initiation, including a three-way handshake; data transfer; and termination.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Connections progress through three phases: initiation, including a three-way handshake; data transfer; and termination.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Connections progress through three phases: initiation, including a three-way handshake; data transfer; and termination.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Every new connection attempt begins with a DCCP-Request packet sent by the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: DCCP-Response: Sent by the server in response to a DCCP-Request (the second part of the three-way initiation handshake).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client sends DCCP-Ack completing the three-way initiation handshake; connection moves to data transfer phase.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: DCCP-CloseReq: Sent by the server to request that the client close the connection (first part of three-way termination handshake).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client sends DCCP-Close in response to DCCP-CloseReq to close the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: DCCP-Close: Used by the client or the server to close the connection; elicits a DCCP-Reset in response.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: DCCP-Reset: Used to terminate the connection, either normally or abnormally.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: DCCP-Sync, DCCP-SyncAck: Used to resynchronize sequence numbers after large bursts of loss.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSED: Represents nonexistent connections. LISTEN and CLOSED are not associated with any particular DCCP connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LISTEN: Represents server sockets in the passive listening state. LISTEN and CLOSED are not associated with any particular DCCP connection.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: REQUEST: A client socket enters this state, from CLOSED, after sending a DCCP-Request packet to try to initiate a connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: RESPOND: A server socket enters this state, from LISTEN, after receiving a DCCP-Request from a client.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: PARTOPEN: A client socket enters this state, from REQUEST, after receiving a DCCP-Response from the server. This state represents the third phase of the three-way handshake. The client may send application data in this state, but it MUST include an Acknowledgement Number on all of its packets.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: OPEN: The central data transfer portion of a DCCP connection. Client and server sockets enter this state from PARTOPEN and RESPOND, respectively. Sometimes we speak of SERVER-OPEN and CLIENT-OPEN states, corresponding to the server's OPEN state and the client's OPEN state.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: CLOSEREQ: A server socket enters this state, from SERVER-OPEN, to order the client to close the connection and to hold TIMEWAIT state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: CLOSING: Server and client sockets can both enter this state to close the connection.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: TIMEWAIT: A server or client socket remains in this state for 2MSL (4 minutes) after the connection has been torn down, to prevent mistakes due to the delivery of old packets. Only one of the endpoints has to enter TIMEWAIT state (the other can enter CLOSED state immediately).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client socket enters REQUEST state, from CLOSED, after sending a DCCP-Request packet to try to initiate a connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server socket enters RESPOND state, from LISTEN, after receiving a DCCP-Request from a client.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client socket enters PARTOPEN state, from REQUEST, after receiving a DCCP-Response from the server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client sockets enter OPEN state from PARTOPEN.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server sockets enter OPEN state from RESPOND.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server socket enters CLOSEREQ state, from SERVER-OPEN, to order the client to close the connection and to hold TIMEWAIT state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client enters CLOSING from OPEN upon receiving DCCP-CloseReq from server (as shown in termination sequence diagram: server in CLOSEREQ sends DCCP-CloseReq, client enters CLOSING and sends DCCP-Close).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server transitions from CLOSEREQ to CLOSED, sending DCCP-Reset, as shown in the typical termination sequence diagram.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client transitions from CLOSING to TIMEWAIT upon receiving DCCP-Reset, as shown in the typical termination sequence diagram.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A server or client socket remains in TIMEWAIT state for 2MSL (4 minutes) after the connection has been torn down, then transitions to CLOSED.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may send application data in PARTOPEN state, but it MUST include an Acknowledgement Number on all of its packets.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Only one of the endpoints has to enter TIMEWAIT state; the other can enter CLOSED state immediately after connection teardown. A server can request its client to hold TIMEWAIT state using the DCCP-CloseReq packet type.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Only one connection endpoint has to hold TIMEWAIT state; the DCCP-CloseReq packet, which may only be sent by the server, passes that state to the client.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The DCCP-CloseReq packet, which may only be sent by the server, passes TIMEWAIT state to the client. Only one connection endpoint has to hold TIMEWAIT state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: DCCP has no states corresponding to TCP's FINWAIT and CLOSEWAIT, where one half-connection is explicitly closed while the other is still active.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client begins in [CLOSED] state at the start of a typical DCCP connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server begins in [LISTEN] state at the start of a typical DCCP connection.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client receives the DCCP-Reset packet and holds state for two maximum segment lifetimes, or 2MSL, to allow any remaining packets to clear the network. [TIMEWAIT]

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client sends the server a DCCP-Request packet specifying the client and server ports, the service being requested, and any features being negotiated.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server sends the client a DCCP-Response packet indicating that it is willing to communicate with the client.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client sends the server a DCCP-Ack packet that acknowledges the DCCP-Response packet. This acknowledges the server's initial sequence number and returns any Init Cookies in the DCCP-Response.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server sends a DCCP-CloseReq packet requesting a close.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client sends a DCCP-Close packet acknowledging the close (in response to DCCP-CloseReq).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server sends a DCCP-Reset packet with Reset Code 1, 'Closed', and clears its connection state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client receives the DCCP-Reset packet and holds state for two maximum segment lifetimes, or 2MSL, to allow any remaining packets to clear the network.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Alternative close: The client sends a DCCP-Close packet closing the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Alternative close: The server sends a DCCP-Reset packet with Reset Code 1, 'Closed', and clears its connection state (in response to client-initiated DCCP-Close).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Alternative close: The client receives the DCCP-Reset packet and holds state for 2MSL to allow any remaining packets to clear the network.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client initiates a DCCP connection by sending a DCCP-Request packet.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server responds to valid DCCP-Request packets with DCCP-Response packets. This is the second phase of the three-way handshake.
actions: send DCCP-Response with Type=1 and X=1
set Service Code equal to Service Code from corresponding DCCP-Request

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Service Code: 32 bits. MUST equal the Service Code on the corresponding DCCP-Request.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Either client or server may send a DCCP-Close packet, which will elicit a DCCP-Reset packet.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Only the server can send a DCCP-CloseReq packet, which indicates that the server wants to close the connection but does not want to hold its TIMEWAIT state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIMEWAIT state referenced as a state the server may or may not hold following connection close; DCCP-CloseReq allows the server to avoid holding TIMEWAIT.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A valid packet arrived with unexpected type. For example, a DCCP-Data packet with valid header checksum and sequence numbers arrived at a connection in the REQUEST state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: DCCP-Reset packets unconditionally shut down a connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A valid packet arrived with unexpected type. For example, a DCCP-Data packet with valid header checksum and sequence numbers arrived at a connection in the REQUEST state. Reset Code 4, Packet Error.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = REQUEST & packet.checksum_valid = true & packet.sequence_numbers_valid = true
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 4 (Packet Error)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Connection Refused: The Destination Port didn't correspond to a port open for listening. Sent only in response to DCCP-Requests.
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 7 (Connection Refused)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Bad Service Code: The Service Code didn't equal the service code attached to the Destination Port. Sent only in response to DCCP-Requests.
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 8 (Bad Service Code)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Too Busy: The server is too busy to accept new connections. Sent only in response to DCCP-Requests.
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 9 (Too Busy)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Options on DCCP-Reset packets are processed before the connection is shut down. This means that certain combinations of options, particularly involving Mandatory, may cause an endpoint to respond to a valid DCCP-Reset with another DCCP-Reset.
statements.trigger: receive DCCP-Reset with Mandatory option error
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 6 (Mandatory Error)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Bad Init Cookie: The Init Cookie echoed by the client was incorrect or missing.
statements.trigger: receive DCCP-Request with incorrect or missing Init Cookie
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 10 (Bad Init Cookie)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Each valid received DCCP-Sync immediately elicits a DCCP-SyncAck.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the endpoint does not understand or process O, however, then it MUST reset the connection using Reset Code 6, "Mandatory Failure".
statements.trigger: Mandatory option received and following option O not understood or not processed
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 6 (Mandatory Failure)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The connection is in error and should be reset with Reset Code 5, "Option Error", if option O is absent (Mandatory was the last byte of the option list), or if option O equals Mandatory.
statements.trigger: Mandatory option received and O is absent or O equals Mandatory
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 5 (Option Error)

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Mandatory options MUST NOT be sent on DCCP-Data packets, and any Mandatory options received on DCCP-Data packets MUST be ignored.
statements.guard_semantics: Mandatory option is prohibited on DCCP-Data packets; if received, must be ignored

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On receiving a Change L option, a DCCP endpoint examines the included preference list, reconciles that with its own preference list, calculates the new value, and sends back a Confirm R option, informing its peer of the new value or that the feature was not understood.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On receiving a Change R option, a DCCP endpoint examines the included preference list, reconciles that with its own preference list, calculates the new value, and sends back a Confirm L option, informing its peer of the new value or that the feature was not understood.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Every non-reordered Change option MUST result in a corresponding Confirm option, and any packet including a Confirm option MUST carry an Acknowledgement Number.
actions: attach Acknowledgement Number to packet carrying Confirm

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The Change-sending endpoint MUST wait to receive a corresponding Confirm option before changing its stored feature value.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The Confirm-sending endpoint changes its stored feature value as soon as it sends the Confirm.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The Change-sending endpoint MUST wait to receive a corresponding Confirm option before changing its stored feature value.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: STABLE is the normal state, where the endpoint knows the feature's value and thinks the other endpoint agrees.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An endpoint enters the CHANGING state when it first sends a Change for the feature and returns to STABLE once it receives a corresponding Confirm.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: UNSTABLE indicates that an endpoint in CHANGING state changed its preference list but has not yet transmitted a Change option with the new preference list.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: app/protocol evt : snd Change L [STABLE -> CHANGING]

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: rcv Confirm R : accept value [CHANGING -> STABLE, nonempty Confirm R with valid value]
statements.pre_cond: F.state = CHANGING & O.type = Confirm_R & O.len > 3 & option.value.valid = true

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: rcv empty Confirm R : revert to old value [CHANGING -> STABLE]

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: rcv Change R : calc new value, snd Confirm L [CHANGING -> STABLE, from diagram arc label and pseudocode step 3 which imposes no state guard]
statements.trigger: receive Change R with valid value
statements.pre_cond: F.state = CHANGING & O.type = Change_R & option.value.valid = true
actions: send Confirm L on a future packet

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: pref list changes [CHANGING -> UNSTABLE]

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: snd Change L [UNSTABLE -> CHANGING]
statements.trigger: send Change L (with new preference list)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: rcv Change R : calc new value, snd Confirm L [STABLE -> STABLE self-loop]
statements.trigger: receive Change R with valid value
statements.pre_cond: F.state = STABLE & O.type = Change_R & option.value.valid = true
actions: send Confirm L on a future packet

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: rcv Confirm R : ignore [STABLE -> STABLE self-loop]

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: timeout/rcv non-ack : snd Change L [CHANGING -> CHANGING self-loop]

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: rcv Confirm/Change R : ignore [UNSTABLE -> UNSTABLE self-loop]
statements.trigger: receive Confirm R or Change R

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If F is unknown and the option was Mandatory, Reset connection and return
statements.trigger: receive Mandatory option for unknown feature

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If F is unknown and O.type == Change R, Send Empty Confirm L on a future packet
statements.trigger: receive Change R for unknown feature (non-Mandatory)
statements.pre_cond: F.unknown = true & O.type = Change_R & option.mandatory = false
actions: send Empty Confirm L on a future packet

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If O.type == Change R, option value is invalid, and option was Mandatory, Reset connection and return
statements.trigger: receive Mandatory Change R with invalid value
statements.pre_cond: O.type = Change_R & option.value.valid = false & option.mandatory = true

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If F.state == CHANGING and O.type == Confirm R and O.len > 3 and the option's value is invalid, Reset connection and return
statements.trigger: receive nonempty Confirm R with invalid value
statements.pre_cond: F.state = CHANGING & O.type = Confirm_R & O.len > 3 & option.value.valid = false

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A CHANGING endpoint transmits another Change option once it realizes that it has not heard back from the other endpoint.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A CHANGING endpoint transmits another Change option once it realizes that it has not heard back from the other endpoint. Endpoints SHOULD use an exponential-backoff timer to decide when to retransmit Change options.
actions: transmit Change option on new packet with new sequence number
apply exponential-backoff timer for next retransmission

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A CHANGING endpoint MUST continue retransmitting Change options until it gets some response or the connection terminates.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A CHANGING endpoint MUST continue retransmitting Change options until it gets some response or the connection terminates.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: STABLE state: a feature negotiation state from which a transition to the CHANGING state can occur when a new Change option is generated.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: UNSTABLE state: a feature negotiation state from which a transition to the CHANGING state can occur when a new Change option is generated.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CHANGING state: feature negotiation state in which Change options are retransmissions and MUST have exactly the same contents as previously transmitted options, allowing tolerance for reordering.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A Change option is new if and only if it was generated during a transition from the STABLE or UNSTABLE state to the CHANGING state.
actions: update FGSS to sent sequence number

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A Change option is new if and only if it was generated during a transition from the STABLE or UNSTABLE state to the CHANGING state.
actions: update FGSS to sent sequence number

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FGSR — Feature Greatest Sequence Number Received: The greatest sequence number received, considering only valid packets that contained one or more feature negotiation options (Change and/or Confirm). This value is initialized to ISR - 1.
statements.guard_semantics: packet.SeqNo <= connection.FGSR implies ignore Change options; packet.SeqNo <= connection.FGSR | !packet.AckNo | packet.AckNo < connection.FGSS implies ignore Confirm options

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FGSS — Feature Greatest Sequence Number Sent: The greatest sequence number sent, considering only packets that contained one or more new Change options. FGSS is initialized to ISS.
statements.guard_semantics: packet.AckNo < connection.FGSS implies ignore Confirm option

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Change options generated within the CHANGING state are retransmissions and MUST have exactly the same contents as previously transmitted options, allowing tolerance for reordering.
actions: retransmit Change option with identical contents to previous transmission

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An endpoint that changes its preference list while in the CHANGING state MUST transition to the UNSTABLE state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An endpoint transitions to the UNSTABLE state when it changes its preference list while in the CHANGING state, and transitions back to CHANGING once it has transmitted a Change option with the new preference list.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An endpoint that changes its preference list while in the CHANGING state MUST transition to the UNSTABLE state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: It will transition back to CHANGING once it has transmitted a Change option with the new preference list.
actions: transmit Change option with new preference list

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An endpoint in the CHANGING state will receive a Change option for the same feature when both endpoints simultaneously open negotiation.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The CHANGING endpoint can then transition to the STABLE state after reconciling preference lists and generating the corresponding Confirm option.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The CHANGING endpoint MUST examine the received Change's preference list, reconcile that with its own preference list (as expressed in its generated Change options), and generate the corresponding Confirm option. It can then transition to the STABLE state.
statements.trigger: received Change option for same feature
actions: reconcile received preference list with own preference list

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: On receiving an empty Confirm option for some feature, the CHANGING endpoint MUST transition back to the STABLE state, leaving the feature's value unchanged.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The CHANGING endpoint that issued a Change option awaits a Confirm; it is in the CHANGING state during feature negotiation.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On receiving an empty Confirm option for some feature, the CHANGING endpoint MUST transition back to the STABLE state, leaving the feature's value unchanged.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: However, if the Change option was Mandatory, the connection MUST be reset.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The CHANGING endpoint SHOULD reset the connection (with Reset Code 5, 'Option Error') if it receives an empty Confirm option for such a feature [required to be understood by all DCCPs].
actions: reset connection with Reset Code 5 (Option Error)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Endpoints MUST respond to unknown Change options with Empty Confirm options (that is, Confirm options containing no data), which inform the CHANGING endpoint that the feature was not understood.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Endpoints MUST ignore any such options they receive [Confirm options referring to a feature number not understood].

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An endpoint receiving an invalid Change option MUST respond with the corresponding empty Confirm option.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An endpoint receiving an invalid Confirm option MUST reset the connection, with Reset Code 5, "Option Error".
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 5 'Option Error'

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Mandatory Change options where the feature number was not understood cause the receiver to reset the connection with Reset Code 6, 'Mandatory Failure'.
statements.trigger: Mandatory Change option received with unknown feature number
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 6 'Mandatory Failure'

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Mandatory Change options where the value was invalid and the receiver would normally have sent an empty Confirm option cause the receiver to reset the connection with Reset Code 6, 'Mandatory Failure'.
statements.trigger: Mandatory Change option received with invalid value (empty Confirm case)
statements.pre_cond: connection.mandatory_change_received = true & connection.change_value_valid = false & connection.would_send_empty_confirm = true
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 6 'Mandatory Failure'

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: For server-priority features, if there was no shared entry in the two endpoints' preference lists, the receiver resets the connection with Reset Code 6, 'Mandatory Failure'.
statements.trigger: Mandatory Change option received with no shared server-priority preference entry
statements.pre_cond: connection.mandatory_change_received = true & connection.feature_type = server_priority & connection.shared_preference_entry = false
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 6 'Mandatory Failure'

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Reordering protection may cause a Mandatory Change option to be ignored without resetting the connection.
statements.trigger: Mandatory Change option received and ignored due to reordering protection

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP endpoints MUST NOT send packets whose sequence numbers are close to the sequence numbers of packets lingering in the network from before the boot. The simplest way to enforce this rule is for DCCP endpoints to avoid sending any packets until one maximum segment lifetime (2 minutes) after boot.
actions: send packets with safe sequence numbers

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Packets whose Sequence and/or Acknowledgement Numbers are out of range are called sequence-invalid and are not processed normally.
statements.guard_semantics: packet.sequence_number = in_range & packet.ack_number = in_range → process_normally; else → sequence_invalid

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A handshake of DCCP-Sync and DCCP-SyncAck packets recovers from large bursts of loss where the other endpoint would label a Sequence Number as invalid.
statements.trigger: sequence-invalid packet received due to large burst of loss

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: New connections start with Sequence Window 100 for both endpoints.
statements.guard_semantics: initial value at connection establishment for both endpoints

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The minimum valid Sequence Window value is Wmin = 32. The maximum valid Sequence Window value is Wmax = 2^46 - 1 = 70368744177663. Change options suggesting Sequence Window values out of this range are invalid and MUST be handled accordingly.
statements.guard_semantics: values outside [Wmin, Wmax] are invalid and must be rejected

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Endpoints SHOULD send Change L(Sequence Window) options, as necessary, as the connection progresses.
statements.trigger: connection progresses / anticipated in-flight packet count changes

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An endpoint MUST NOT persistently send more than its Sequence Window number of packets per round-trip time; that is, DCCP A MUST NOT persistently send more than Sequence Window/A packets per RTT.
statements.trigger: packet send rate exceeds Sequence Window / RTT
actions: cease persistent over-sending beyond Sequence Window/A per RTT

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Check not applied if connection is in LISTEN or REQUEST state. (Referring to DCCP-Request and DCCP-Response sequence number check SWL <= seqno <= SWH.)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Check not applied if connection is in LISTEN or REQUEST state. (Referring to DCCP-Request and DCCP-Response sequence number check SWL <= seqno <= SWH.)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The sequence number check (SWL <= seqno <= SWH) for DCCP-Request and DCCP-Response packets is not applied if the connection is in LISTEN or REQUEST state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Endpoints in an unsynchronized state (CLOSED, REQUEST, and LISTEN) might not have enough information to generate a proper DCCP-Reset on the first try.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Endpoints in an unsynchronized state (CLOSED, REQUEST, and LISTEN) might not have enough information to generate a proper DCCP-Reset on the first try.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Endpoints in an unsynchronized state (CLOSED, REQUEST, and LISTEN) might not have enough information to generate a proper DCCP-Reset on the first try.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Any sequence-invalid DCCP-Sync or DCCP-SyncAck packet MUST be ignored.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A sequence-invalid DCCP-Reset packet MUST elicit a DCCP-Sync packet in response (subject to a possible rate limit). This response packet MUST use a new Sequence Number, and thus will increase GSS; GSR will not change, however, since the received packet was sequence-invalid. The response packet's Acknowledgement Number MUST equal GSR.
actions: send DCCP-Sync with new Sequence Number

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Any other sequence-invalid packet MUST elicit a similar DCCP-Sync packet, except that the response packet's Acknowledgement Number MUST equal the sequence-invalid packet's Sequence Number.
actions: send DCCP-Sync with new Sequence Number

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On receiving a sequence-valid DCCP-Sync packet, the peer endpoint MUST update its GSR variable and reply with a DCCP-SyncAck packet. The DCCP-SyncAck packet's Acknowledgement Number will equal the DCCP-Sync's Sequence Number.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: As an exception, if the peer endpoint is in the REQUEST state, it MUST respond with a DCCP-Reset instead of a DCCP-SyncAck. This serves to clean up DCCP A's half-open connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: any options whose processing might cause the connection to be reset are ignored when they appear on DCCP-Data packets
statements.trigger: received DCCP-Data packet containing options that might cause connection reset
actions: ignore reset-triggering options on DCCP-Data packet

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: CLOSED state of DCCP A after a crash, before reconnection attempt in the half-open connection recovery example.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: OPEN state of DCCP B during the half-open connection recovery example, representing an established connection.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: REQUEST state of DCCP A during the half-open connection recovery example, representing an in-progress connection initiation.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: After a crash, DCCP A transitions from CLOSED to REQUEST by sending a DCCP-Request (half-open recovery example: DCCP-Request(seq 400)).
statements.trigger: local application open request after crash

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP B, in OPEN state, receives a DCCP-Request whose sequence number is out of the appropriate sequence number window, and responds by sending a DCCP-Sync; DCCP B remains in OPEN.
statements.trigger: receive DCCP-Request with seqno out of range
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = OPEN & received_seqno out of appropriate_sequence_number_window

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP A, in REQUEST state, receives DCCP-Sync from DCCP B (half-open peer) and responds by sending DCCP-Reset; DCCP A remains in REQUEST.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP B, in OPEN state, receives DCCP-Reset from DCCP A and aborts, transitioning to CLOSED (half-open connection recovery).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP B, whose sequence number is out of DCCP A's appropriate sequence number window after a burst of loss, sends a DCCP-Sync; upon receiving DCCP-SyncAck, both sides update GSS/GSR state (first burst-loss example).
statements.trigger: receive packet with seqno out of appropriate sequence number window

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP A receives DCCP-Sync with an acknowledgement number out of range (from attacker-injected packet causing DCCP B to send Sync) and ignores it; state is unchanged.
statements.trigger: receive DCCP-Sync with ackno out of range

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: After DCCP B aborts and closes due to receiving Reset in the half-open recovery example, DCCP A (still in REQUEST) retransmits DCCP-Request to re-establish the connection.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client State: CLOSED — initial state before connection establishment, as shown in the connection establishment diagram.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client moves from the REQUEST state to PARTOPEN, and finally to OPEN.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client moves from the REQUEST state to PARTOPEN, and finally to OPEN.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The client moves from the REQUEST state to PARTOPEN, and finally to OPEN; the server moves from LISTEN to RESPOND, and finally to OPEN.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server State: LISTEN — initial state for the server side before connection establishment, as shown in the connection establishment diagram.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server moves from LISTEN to RESPOND, and finally to OPEN.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client initiates connection by sending initial DCCP-Request packet, moving from CLOSED to REQUEST.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server moves from LISTEN to RESPOND upon receiving DCCP-Request from client, sending DCCP-Response in reply.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client moves from the REQUEST state to PARTOPEN upon receiving DCCP-Response, sending acknowledgement via DCCP-Ack or DCCP-DataAck.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server moves from RESPOND to OPEN upon receiving Ack or DataAck from client in PARTOPEN.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client moves from PARTOPEN to OPEN upon receiving Data, Ack, or DataAck from the server once the server has entered OPEN.
statements.trigger: receive Data, Ack, or DataAck from server in OPEN

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When a client decides to initiate a connection, it enters the REQUEST state

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When a client decides to initiate a connection, it enters the REQUEST state, chooses an initial sequence number, and sends a DCCP-Request packet using that sequence number to the intended server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client in the REQUEST state SHOULD use an exponential-backoff timer to send new DCCP-Request packets if no response is received.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client MAY give up on its DCCP-Requests after some time (3 minutes, for example). When it does, it SHOULD send a DCCP-Reset packet to the server with Reset Code 2, 'Aborted', to clean up state in case one or more of the Requests actually arrived.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client leaves the REQUEST state for PARTOPEN when it receives a DCCP-Response from the server.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the DCCP-Request's Service Code doesn't equal any of the server's Service Codes for the given port, the server MUST reject the request by sending a DCCP-Reset packet with Reset Code 8, "Bad Service Code".
statements.trigger: DCCP-Request received with non-matching Service Code
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 8 (Bad Service Code)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST reject any DCCP-Request with Service Code value 4294967295 by sending a DCCP-Reset packet with Reset Code 8, "Bad Service Code".
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 8 (Bad Service Code)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Each DCCP-Request contains a 32-bit Service Code, which identifies the application-level service to which the client application is trying to connect.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Endpoints MUST associate a Service Code with every DCCP socket, both actively and passively opened. Each active socket MUST have exactly one Service Code.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the second phase of the three-way handshake, the server moves from the LISTEN state to RESPOND and sends a DCCP-Response message to the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY respond to a DCCP-Request packet with a DCCP-Reset packet to refuse the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Every valid DCCP-Request received while the server is in the RESPOND state MUST elicit a new DCCP-Response.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server leaves the RESPOND state for OPEN when it receives a valid DCCP-Ack from the client, completing the three-way handshake.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MAY also leave the RESPOND state for CLOSED after a timeout of not less than 4MSL (8 minutes); when doing so, it SHOULD send a DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 2, "Aborted", to clean up state at the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the second phase of the three-way handshake, the server moves from the LISTEN state to RESPOND.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server leaves the RESPOND state for OPEN when it receives a valid DCCP-Ack from the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MAY also leave the RESPOND state for CLOSED after a timeout of not less than 4MSL (8 minutes).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Init Cookie option lets a DCCP server avoid having to hold any state until the three-way connection setup handshake has completed. In the meantime, it need not move from the LISTEN state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Any Init Cookie options received ... after the connection has been established (when the connection's state is >= OPEN), MUST be ignored.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It need not move from the LISTEN state [while using Init Cookie to avoid holding state until the three-way connection setup handshake has completed].
statements.trigger: DCCP-Request received with Init Cookie mechanism active
actions: send DCCP-Response with Init Cookie option

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Any Init Cookie options received on DCCP-Request or DCCP-Data packets, or after the connection has been established (when the connection's state is >= OPEN), MUST be ignored.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD respond to a tampered Init Cookie option by resetting the connection with Reset Code 10, 'Bad Init Cookie'.
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 10 (Bad Init Cookie)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST echo the same Init Cookie options, in the same order, in each succeeding DCCP packet until one of those packets is acknowledged (showing that the three-way handshake has completed) or the connection is reset.
actions: echo Init Cookie options in every outgoing packet until acknowledged

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST NOT use DCCP-Data packets until the three-way handshake completes or the connection is reset.
statements.guard_semantics: DCCP-Data packets prohibited while three-way handshake incomplete and Init Cookie in use

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Init Cookie option MUST NOT be sent on DCCP-Request or DCCP-Data packets.
statements.guard_semantics: Init Cookie option forbidden on DCCP-Request and DCCP-Data packet types

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client moves from the REQUEST state to PARTOPEN and completes the three-way handshake by sending a DCCP-Ack packet to the server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the client receives a DCCP-Response from the server, it moves from the REQUEST state to PARTOPEN and completes the three-way handshake by sending a DCCP-Ack packet to the server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client leaves the PARTOPEN state for OPEN when it receives a valid packet other than DCCP-Response, DCCP-Reset, or DCCP-Sync from the server.
statements.trigger: receive valid packet other than DCCP-Response, DCCP-Reset, or DCCP-Sync
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = PARTOPEN & received_packet != DCCP-Response & received_packet != DCCP-Reset & received_packet != DCCP-Sync

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client remains in PARTOPEN for more than 4MSL (8 minutes), it SHOULD reset the connection with Reset Code 2, Aborted.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The preferred mechanism would be a roughly 200-millisecond timer, set every time a packet is transmitted in PARTOPEN. If this timer goes off and the client is still in PARTOPEN, the client generates another DCCP-Ack and backs off the timer.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients in the PARTOPEN state that want to send data MUST do so using DCCP-DataAck packets, not DCCP-Data packets.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the DCCP-Response included an Init Cookie, that Init Cookie MUST be included on every packet sent in PARTOPEN.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the central data transfer phase of the connection, both server and client are in the OPEN state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On receiving a valid DCCP-Sync packet, a DCCP endpoint MUST immediately generate and send a DCCP-SyncAck response (subject to any implementation rate limits); the Acknowledgement Number on that DCCP-SyncAck MUST equal the Sequence Number of the DCCP-Sync.
actions: set DCCP-SyncAck Acknowledgement Number = received DCCP-Sync Sequence Number

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A particular DCCP implementation might decide to initiate feature negotiation only once the OPEN state was reached, in which case it might not allow data transfer until some time later. Data received during that time SHOULD be rejected and reported using a Data Dropped Drop Block with Drop Code 0, Protocol Constraints.
statements.trigger: receive data before feature negotiation complete
actions: send Data Dropped Drop Block with Drop Code 0 (Protocol Constraints)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The server moves from the OPEN state, possibly through the CLOSEREQ state, to CLOSED; the client moves from OPEN through CLOSING to TIMEWAIT.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server moves from the OPEN state, possibly through the CLOSEREQ state, to CLOSED. Only the server can send a DCCP-CloseReq packet or enter the CLOSEREQ state. Endpoints in the CLOSEREQ state MUST retransmit DCCP-CloseReq packets until leaving that state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The client moves from OPEN through CLOSING to TIMEWAIT. Endpoints in the CLOSING state MUST retransmit DCCP-Close packets until leaving that state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: TIMEWAIT state, where an endpoint quietly preserves a socket for 2MSL (4 minutes) after its connection has closed, ensures that no connection duplicating the current connection's source and destination addresses and ports can start up while old packets might remain in the network.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: DCCP implementations generally transition to the CLOSED state after sending a DCCP-Reset packet.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Scenario 1, step 1: Server moves from OPEN to CLOSEREQ and sends DCCP-CloseReq when it decides to close the connection without holding TIMEWAIT state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Scenario 1, step 2: Client moves from OPEN to CLOSING upon receiving DCCP-CloseReq, and sends DCCP-Close.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Scenario 1, step 3: Server moves from CLOSEREQ to CLOSED upon receiving DCCP-Close, and sends DCCP-Reset.
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 1 Closed

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Scenarios 1 and 2: Client moves from CLOSING to TIMEWAIT upon receiving DCCP-Reset.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Scenarios 1 and 2: Client moves from TIMEWAIT to CLOSED after 2MSL wait time (4 minutes).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Scenario 2, step 1: Client moves from OPEN to CLOSING and sends DCCP-Close when it decides to close the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Scenario 2, step 2: Server moves from OPEN to CLOSED upon receiving DCCP-Close, and sends DCCP-Reset.
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 1 Closed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Scenario 3, step 1: Server moves from OPEN to CLOSING and sends DCCP-Close when it decides to hold TIMEWAIT state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Scenario 3, step 2: Client moves from OPEN to CLOSED upon receiving DCCP-Close, and sends DCCP-Reset.
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 1 Closed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Scenario 3, step 3: Server moves from CLOSING to TIMEWAIT upon receiving DCCP-Reset.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Scenario 3, step 4: Server moves from TIMEWAIT to CLOSED after 2MSL wait time (4 minutes).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The receiver of a valid DCCP-CloseReq packet MUST respond with a DCCP-Close packet.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The receiver of a valid DCCP-Close packet MUST respond with a DCCP-Reset packet with Reset Code 1, "Closed".
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 1 Closed

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The receiver of a valid DCCP-Reset packet will hold TIMEWAIT state for the connection. The endpoint that receives a valid DCCP-Reset SHOULD hold TIMEWAIT state for the connection.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP implementations generally transition to the CLOSED state after sending a DCCP-Reset packet.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server receiving a sequence-valid DCCP-CloseReq packet MUST respond with a DCCP-Sync packet and otherwise ignore the DCCP-CloseReq.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Only the server can send a DCCP-CloseReq packet or enter the CLOSEREQ state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Endpoints in the CLOSEREQ and CLOSING states MUST retransmit DCCP-CloseReq and DCCP-Close packets, respectively, until leaving those states. The retransmission timer should initially be set to go off in two round-trip times and should back off to not less than once every 64 seconds if no relevant response is received.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Resets sent in the CLOSED state use Reset Code 3, 'No Connection', unless otherwise specified. This state has no associated sequence number variables.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Resets sent in the LISTEN state use Reset Code 3, 'No Connection', unless otherwise specified. This state has no associated sequence number variables.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Resets sent in the TIMEWAIT state use Reset Code 3, 'No Connection', unless otherwise specified. This state has no associated sequence number variables.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Resets sent in the REQUEST state use Reset Code 4, 'Packet Error', unless otherwise specified.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Resets sent in the RESPOND state use Reset Code 4, 'Packet Error', unless otherwise specified.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP endpoints generate DCCP-Reset packets to terminate connections abnormally; a DCCP-Reset packet may be generated from any state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Resets sent in the CLOSED, LISTEN, and TIMEWAIT states use Reset Code 3, 'No Connection', unless otherwise specified.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = CLOSED | protocol.state = LISTEN | protocol.state = TIMEWAIT
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 3 (No Connection)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Resets sent in the REQUEST or RESPOND states use Reset Code 4, 'Packet Error', unless otherwise specified.
actions: send DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 4 (Packet Error)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP endpoints in CLOSED, LISTEN, or TIMEWAIT state may need to generate a DCCP-Reset packet in response to a packet received from a peer. Since these states have no associated sequence number variables, the Sequence and Acknowledgement Numbers on the DCCP-Reset packet R are taken from the received packet P.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = CLOSED | protocol.state = LISTEN | protocol.state = TIMEWAIT
actions: if P.ackno exists then set R.seqno := P.ackno + 1 else set R.seqno := 0
if P.X = 0 then set upper 24 bits of R.seqno and R.ackno to 0

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSED state as shown in the DCCP state diagram; the initial and final resting state of a DCCP connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LISTEN state as shown in the DCCP state diagram; server is passively awaiting an incoming connection request.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: REQUEST state as shown in the DCCP state diagram; client has sent a DCCP-Request and is awaiting a DCCP-Response.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: RESPOND state as shown in the DCCP state diagram; server has received a DCCP-Request and sent a DCCP-Response, awaiting an Ack.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: PARTOPEN state as shown in the DCCP state diagram; client has sent a DCCP-Ack and is waiting to confirm the connection is fully open.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: OPEN state as shown in the DCCP state diagram; connection is fully established and data transfer is active.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSEREQ state as shown in the DCCP state diagram; server has initiated closing by sending a DCCP-CloseReq.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSING state as shown in the DCCP state diagram; endpoint has sent a DCCP-Close and is awaiting a DCCP-Reset.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIMEWAIT state as shown in the DCCP state diagram; endpoint is waiting for the 2MSL timer to expire before transitioning to CLOSED.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: passive open: server moves from CLOSED to LISTEN.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: active open: client moves from CLOSED to REQUEST, sending a DCCP-Request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: server receives DCCP-Request and sends DCCP-Response, moving from LISTEN to RESPOND.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: client receives DCCP-Response and sends DCCP-Ack, moving from REQUEST to PARTOPEN.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: server receives DCCP-Ack or DCCP-DataAck, moving from RESPOND to OPEN.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: client receives a packet from the server, moving from PARTOPEN to OPEN.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: server active close: server sends DCCP-CloseReq and moves from OPEN to CLOSEREQ.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: active close or receipt of DCCP-CloseReq: endpoint sends DCCP-Close and moves from OPEN to CLOSING.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: endpoint in OPEN receives a DCCP-Close, sends DCCP-Reset, and moves directly to CLOSED (center path in state diagram).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: server in CLOSEREQ receives a DCCP-Close, sends DCCP-Reset, and moves to CLOSED.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: endpoint in CLOSING receives a DCCP-Reset and moves to TIMEWAIT.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: 2MSL timer expires in TIMEWAIT; connection moves to CLOSED.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: There are arcs (not shown) from every state except CLOSED to TIMEWAIT, contingent on the receipt of a valid DCCP-Reset.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 2: If no socket, or S.state == TIMEWAIT, generate Reset(No Connection) unless P.type == Reset, drop packet and return

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 3: Process LISTEN state — if S.state == LISTEN and P.type == Request or P contains a valid Init Cookie option, create new socket and set S.state = RESPOND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 4: Process REQUEST state — if S.state == REQUEST, only Response and Reset are valid; otherwise generate Reset(Packet Error) and drop

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 11: Process RESPOND state — if S.state == RESPOND, process Request by sending Response, or set S.state := OPEN on other valid packet types

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 12: Process PARTOPEN state — PARTOPEN means send an Ack, don't send Data packets, retransmit Acks periodically, and always include any Init Cookie from the Response

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 7 references S.state >= OPEN as a threshold for detecting unexpected Request and Response packets; Steps 11 and 12 transition into OPEN

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 13 uses S.state < CLOSEREQ as the guard for transitioning to CLOSING on receipt of CloseReq

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 13: S.state := CLOSING is set when CloseReq is received and S.state < CLOSEREQ; Set CLOSING timer

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 3: If S.state == LISTEN and (P.type == Request or P contains a valid Init Cookie option), generate a new socket, set S.state = RESPOND, initialize sequence number variables
statements.trigger: receive Request or valid Init Cookie
actions: create new socket for this port pair
choose S.ISS or set from Init Cookies
set S.ISR, S.GSR, S.SWL, S.SWH from packet or Init Cookies

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 11: If S.state == RESPOND and P.type == Request, send Response possibly containing Init Cookie; if Init Cookie was sent, destroy socket and return
actions: send Response possibly containing Init Cookie
if Init Cookie sent: destroy socket and return

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 11: If S.state == RESPOND and P.type != Request (Otherwise branch), set S.OSR := P.seqno, S.state := OPEN

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 10: If S.state == REQUEST and P is a valid Response (Step 4 passed), S.state := PARTOPEN; Set PARTOPEN timer; continue with S.state == PARTOPEN
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = REQUEST & P.type = Response & S.AWL <= P.ackno & P.ackno <= S.AWH

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 12: If S.state == PARTOPEN and P.type == Response, send Ack (no state change)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 12: If S.state == PARTOPEN and P.type != Response and P.type != Sync, set S.OSR := P.seqno, S.state := OPEN
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = PARTOPEN & P.type != Response & P.type != Sync

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 9: If P.type == Reset, tear down connection, S.state := TIMEWAIT, set TIMEWAIT timer, drop packet and return

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 2: If S.state == TIMEWAIT, generate Reset(No Connection) unless P.type == Reset, drop packet and return (state unchanged)
actions: generate Reset(No Connection) if P.type != Reset

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 13: If P.type == CloseReq and S.state < CLOSEREQ, generate Close, S.state := CLOSING, set CLOSING timer

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step 14: If P.type == Close, generate Reset(Closed), tear down connection, drop packet and return

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: New connections start with Minimum Checksum Coverage 0 for both endpoints.
statements.guard_semantics: initial value at connection start for both endpoints

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Reset Codes 128 through 191 indicate that the HC-Sender reset the connection (most likely because of some problem with acknowledgements sent by the HC-Receiver).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Reset Codes 192 through 255 indicate that the HC-Receiver reset the connection (most likely because of some problem with data packets sent by the HC-Sender).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: if a DCCP-Request contains the option sequence 'Mandatory, Change L(CCID, 3), 128', then either the '128' option will be processed by CCID 3 or the connection will be reset.
statements.trigger: Mandatory Change(CCID) followed by CCID-specific option where CCID not supported

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST treat such options as non-understood. Thus, it will reset the connection on encountering a Mandatory CCID-specific option or feature negotiation request.
statements.trigger: receive Mandatory CCID-specific option or feature negotiation (non-understood)
statements.pre_cond: server.implements_ccid2 = false & option.mandatory = true & option.ccid_specific = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: send an empty Confirm for a non-Mandatory Change option for a CCID-specific feature
statements.trigger: receive non-Mandatory Change option for CCID-specific feature (non-understood)
statements.pre_cond: server.implements_ccid2 = false & option.mandatory = false & option.type = Change & option.ccid_specific = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: ignore other CCID-specific options
statements.trigger: receive other CCID-specific option (non-understood, non-mandatory, non-Change)
statements.pre_cond: server.implements_ccid2 = false & option.mandatory = false & option.ccid_specific = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers that do not implement the default CCID 2 might nevertheless receive CCID 2-specific options on a DCCP-Request packet. Such a server MUST send Mandatory Change(CCID) options on its DCCP-Response.
statements.trigger: send DCCP-Response when server does not implement CCID 2
actions: include Mandatory Change(CCID) options in DCCP-Response

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: DCCP was designed to work well for both bidirectional and unidirectional flows of data, and for connections that transition between these states.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: DCCP was designed to work well for both bidirectional and unidirectional flows of data, and for connections that transition between these states.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP B goes 'quiescent'. This means that the connection becomes unidirectional: DCCP B stops sending data and sends only DCCP-Ack packets to DCCP A.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP A switches its ack pattern from bidirectional to unidirectional when it notices that DCCP B has gone quiescent.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: It switches from unidirectional to bidirectional when it must acknowledge even a single DCCP-Data or DCCP-DataAck packet from DCCP B.
statements.trigger: receive DCCP-Data or DCCP-DataAck from peer

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: One or more Ack Vector options that, together, report the status of a packet with a sequence number less than ISN, the initial sequence number, SHOULD be considered invalid. The receiving DCCP SHOULD either ignore the options or reset the connection with Reset Code 5, "Option Error".
statements.trigger: AckVector option references sequence number less than ISN
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 5 Option Error

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Ack Vector State 0: the packet was received and is not ECN-marked (received non-marked).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Ack Vector State 1: the packet was received and is ECN-marked (received ECN marked).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Ack Vector State 3: the packet was not received.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The HC-Receiver received packet 24 between sending its acks, so the first ack said 24 was not received (State 3) and the second said it was received or ECN marked (State 0 or 1).
actions: update Ack Vector entry to State 0

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The HC-Receiver received packet 24 between sending its acks, so the first ack said 24 was not received (State 3) and the second said it was received or ECN marked (State 0 or 1).
actions: update Ack Vector entry to State 1

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The HC-Receiver received packet 24 between sending its acks, and the network reordered the acks. In this case, the packet will appear to transition from State 0 or 1 to State 3.
actions: update Ack Vector entry to State 3 due to reordering

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The HC-Receiver received packet 24 between sending its acks, and the network reordered the acks. In this case, the packet will appear to transition from State 0 or 1 to State 3.
actions: update Ack Vector entry to State 3 due to reordering

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The network duplicated packet 24, and one of the duplicates was ECN marked. This might show up as a transition between States 0 and 1.
actions: update Ack Vector entry to State 1 due to ECN-marked duplicate

statements.subject: message
statements.description: HC-Sender combining table: old state 3, received state 0 yields new state 0. Allows the HC-Sender to undo its reaction to presumed congestion when a lost packet unexpectedly shows up (the transition from State 3 to State 0).
actions: combine Ack Vector states to new state 0

statements.subject: message
statements.description: HC-Sender combining table: old state 3, received state 1 yields new state 1.
actions: combine Ack Vector states to new state 1

statements.subject: message
statements.description: HC-Sender combining table: old state 1, received state 3 yields new state 1 (State 1 is sticky against State 3).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: HC-Sender combining table: old state 0, received state 3 yields new state 0 (State 0 is sticky against State 3 at sender).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: HC-Receiver stored-state table: stored state 1, received packet state 0 yields new stored state 0 or 1. The receiver is allowed to switch its stored state to 0.
actions: update stored Ack Vector state to 0

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: One or more Data Dropped options that, together, report the status of more packets than have been sent, or that change the status of a packet, or that disagree with Ack Vector or equivalent options SHOULD be considered invalid. The receiving DCCP SHOULD either ignore such options, or respond by resetting the connection with Reset Code 5, 'Option Error'.
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 5 (Option Error)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: New connections start with ECN Incapable 0 (that is, ECN capable) for both endpoints.
statements.guard_semantics: Initial value at connection start for both endpoints

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If a DCCP is not ECN capable, it MUST send Mandatory 'Change L(ECN Incapable, 1)' options to the other endpoint until acknowledged (by 'Confirm R(ECN Incapable, 1)') or the connection closes.
statements.trigger: Confirm R(ECN Incapable, 1) received | connection closes

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: it MUST NOT accept any data until the other endpoint sends 'Confirm R(ECN Incapable, 1)'. It SHOULD send Data Dropped options on its acknowledgements, with Drop Code 0 ('protocol constraints'), if the other endpoint does send data inappropriately.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the ECN Incapable/A feature is one, then all of DCCP B's packets MUST be sent as ECN incapable.
statements.guard_semantics: When ECN Incapable/A = 1, peer MUST send all packets as ECN incapable

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An entity that detects particularly egregious and ongoing misbehavior MAY also reset the connection with Reset Code 11, "Aggression Penalty".
statements.trigger: detection of egregious and ongoing congestion-related misbehavior
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 11 (Aggression Penalty)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A connection MAY be reset with Reset Code 11, 'Aggression Penalty', if one endpoint determines that the other is reporting a much-too-large Elapsed Time.
actions: send Reset with Reset Code 11 (Aggression Penalty)
